historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Beta-lactamase inhibitors

starting.description: Recognized bacterial penicillinase-mediated antibiotic destruction and prior β-lactamase inhibition by a microbial metabolite, cephalosporin C, supported a purposeful microbial search for inhibitors; the observed activity of a S. clavuligerus culture supplied the clavulanic acid lead.

inspiration.description: Bacterial β-lactamase-mediated resistance and inhibition by the microbial metabolite cephalosporin C provided a rationale and precedent for the microbial search; a distinct natural product isolated from S. clavuligerus supplied the clavulanic acid lead. Observed effects of semisynthetic penicillins motivated a parallel screen of existing compounds, not a claim that clavulanic acid itself was derived from them.

steps.description: Observed bacterial destruction of penicillins and inhibition of penicillinase by a microbial metabolite and some semisynthetic penicillins established the protecting-inhibitor rationale.
In a parallel line, investigators screened semisynthetic penicillins for better inhibition; a promising lead proved poorly absorbed orally.
Rolinson began a synergy screen for natural inhibitors in 1967; the programme initially found unstable olivanic-acid activity.
A cephamycin-related hypothesis led the team to grow S. clavuligerus, where chromatography detected the distinct inhibitory product later named clavulanic acid.

The team pursued a penicillin-plus-inhibitor strategy; the observed inhibitor lowered the in-vitro antibiotic concentrations needed against several resistant strains, and favorable oral absorption was discovered during development.
Clavulanic acid was introduced in an amoxicillin combination in 1981, followed by a ticarcillin combination.

design.description: Researchers designed and adapted the synergy screen, selected and cultured a producer organism, separated the inhibitor from culture fluid, and planned penicillin-plus-inhibitor therapy. The lead's biological activity and favorable absorption were observed rather than specified de novo.

circumstances.description: The search for microbial enzyme inhibitors and the therapeutic combination were planned. Cole describes obtaining a culture to explore cephamycins but identifying a different inhibitor, and Doyle calls the compatible oral absorption a fortunate finding.

limits: This record's founding conclusion concerns the clavulanic acid natural-product path, not all later β-lactamase inhibitor architectures.
Earlier olivanic-acid and semisynthetic-penicillin inhibitor observations are preserved as context and antecedents; their later clinical development is not assumed.
conflicts: E5 and E11: the 1976 Brown report and Rolinson's 1998 account describe K. aerogenes in the assay, whereas Cole's 1998 recollection in E2 names Klebsiella pneumoniae. Whether different screening stages or a naming/recollection discrepancy explain this is unresolved.

E13 versus E6 and E8: the 2007 abstract names Streptococcus clavuligerus as the producer, whereas the contemporary reports name Streptomyces clavuligerus. The reason for the conflicting genus is not established.
gaps: The 1977 original report was read only in abstract; its full experimental details were not inspected.
The 1956 cephalosporin C and 1972 semisynthetic-penicillin primary reports were not read; their observations and the programme's use of them are presented through Cole's retrospective.
